subject: BPSC E-Trap & D-Trap Special Confusion Drill
exam_relevance: High-frequency BPSC TRE 5-option trap drill (targeting None of the above & More than one of the above)

questions.question: What is the maximum decimal digit that can be represented in a single 4-bit 8421 BCD code?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Single-digit 8421 BCD represents only 0–9 (max is 9). Codes 1010–1111 (10–15) are invalid in BCD.

questions.question: Which 4-bit Gray code corresponds to the binary number 1010?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Binary 1010 to Gray: G3=1, G2=1^0=1, G1=0^1=1, G0=1^0=1, giving 1111. None of A/B/C is 1111.

questions.question: Which of the following logic gates are classified as universal gates?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both NAND (A) and NOR (B) are universal gates capable of implementing any Boolean function; XOR is not.

questions.question: In a 4-bit R-2R ladder DAC with Vref = 5 V, what is the step size (LSB weight = Vref / 2^n)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: For a 4-bit DAC, step size = 5 / 2^4 = 5 / 16 = 0.3125 V. None of 0.50 V, 1.25 V, or 0.25 V matches.

questions.question: How many clock cycles does an n-bit Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC require per conversion?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An n-bit SAR ADC performs binary search bit by bit and takes exactly n clock cycles (not 2^n or n^2).

questions.question: Which statements are true regarding a JK flip-flop?

options.A: J=1, K=1 toggles the output on an active clock trigger
options.B: J=0, K=0 holds the previous output state
options.C: Level-triggered JK suffers from race-around if clock pulse exceeds propagation delay
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements (A, B, and C) accurately describe standard JK flip-flop behavior.

questions.question: For a 4-input AND gate, how many rows in its truth table produce a HIGH (1) output?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Out of 16 rows in a 4-input AND truth table, only 1 row (1111) outputs 1; the other 15 rows output 0.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of 2-input NAND gates required to implement an XOR gate (A ⊕ B)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Implementing 2-input XOR requires a minimum of 4 two-input NAND gates (XNOR requires 5).

questions.question: In 8-bit 2's complement signed representation, what is the valid decimal range?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 8-bit 2's complement range is -2^7 to +(2^7 - 1), which is -128 to +127. None of A/B/C matches.

questions.question: Which of the following 4-bit binary codes are self-complementing codes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both Excess-3 (A) and 2421 (B) are self-complementing (9's complement via bitwise inversion); 8421 BCD is not.

questions.question: A MOD-16 asynchronous ripple counter requires at least how many flip-flops?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A MOD-N counter needs ceil(log2(N)) flip-flops: for MOD-16, 2^4 = 16, so 4 flip-flops are required.

questions.question: Which of the following Boolean identities represent De Morgan's laws?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both A and B are De Morgan's theorems; C is incorrect.

questions.question: How many select lines are required for a 32-to-1 multiplexer (MUX)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A 2^n-to-1 MUX requires n select lines; since 32 = 2^5, exactly 5 select lines are needed.

questions.question: Which analog-to-digital converter (ADC) architecture provides the fastest conversion speed?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Flash ADC uses 2^n - 1 comparators in parallel to convert an analog input in a single step (fastest).

questions.question: Which characteristics belong to combinational logic circuits (unlike sequential circuits)?

options.A: Outputs depend solely on the present combination of inputs
options.B: Contain no memory elements or feedback paths
options.C: Require a global clock pulse for state transitions
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Combinational circuits depend only on present inputs (A) and have no memory/feedback (B); clocks belong to sequential circuits.

questions.question: In C++, what are the default access specifiers for members of a class and a struct, respectively?

options.A: public for class, private for struct
options.B: public for both class and struct
options.C: private for both class and struct
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In C++, class members are private by default while struct members are public by default.

questions.question: Which of the following C++ functions CANNOT be declared using the virtual keyword?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Constructors, static member functions, and friend functions cannot be virtual in C++ (all three A, B, C).

questions.question: In standard C++, what does sizeof(Empty) evaluate to for an empty class 'class Empty {};'?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: sizeof an empty class is never 0; C++ assigns it 1 byte (nonzero) so separate instances get unique addresses.

questions.question: In 16-bit Turbo C++ (frequently tested in BPSC TRE), what are the sizes of 'int' and 'long double'?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In 16-bit Turbo C++, int occupies 2 bytes and long double occupies 10 bytes. None of A/B/C matches.

questions.question: Which statements are true about a 'friend' function in C++?

options.A: It can access private and protected members of the class
options.B: It is not in class scope and has no 'this' pointer
options.C: Friendship is automatically inherited by derived classes
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Friend functions can access private/protected members (A) and lack a 'this' pointer (B); friendship is not inherited.

questions.question: Which C++ file stream mode ensures every write operation always appends to the end of the file?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ios::app forces all writes to the end of the file. ios::ate only positions at end on open and allows seeking elsewhere.

questions.question: Which of the following C++ operators CANNOT be overloaded?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: :: (scope resolution), . (dot), .* (member pointer), ?: (ternary), and sizeof cannot be overloaded in C++.

questions.question: When deleting a Derived object through a Base pointer (Base *p = new Derived; delete p;), what ensures ~Derived() runs?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Declaring the BASE class destructor 'virtual' ensures ~Derived() executes before ~Base() on polymorphic delete.

questions.question: Which statements are true regarding pure virtual functions and abstract classes in C++?

options.A: A pure virtual function is declared using '= 0' in the base class
options.B: Objects of an abstract class cannot be instantiated directly
options.C: A derived class that omits overriding a pure virtual function remains abstract
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements (A, B, C) are valid rules for pure virtual functions and abstract classes in C++.

questions.question: In C++, if two functions in the same scope differ ONLY in their return type (identical name and parameters), what occurs?

options.A: Compiler resolves the call from the assignment target type
options.B: The first declared function is always invoked
options.C: Both functions execute sequentially at runtime
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: It triggers a compile-time error: functions cannot be overloaded solely by return type in C++.

questions.question: Which C++ operators can be overloaded as non-static class member functions?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three operators (=, [], and ()) can — and must — be overloaded as non-static member functions in C++.

questions.question: In C++, if class B inherits from class A using protected inheritance (class B : protected A), public members of A become:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: With protected inheritance, public and protected members of A become protected members inside B.

questions.question: In C++, what is the default argument-passing mechanism for fundamental types such as int or double?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: C++ passes scalar arguments by value by default (making a copy); reference (&) or pointer (*) must be explicit.

questions.question: Which C++ keyword allows a specific data member of a class to be modified even inside a const member function?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The 'mutable' keyword lets a non-static data member be modified inside const member functions.

questions.question: Which statements accurately describe destructors in C++?

options.A: A class can have only one destructor and it takes no arguments
options.B: Destructors are called in reverse order of constructor execution
options.C: A class can overload multiple destructors with different parameters
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A class has one parameterless destructor (A), invoked in reverse order of construction (B); destructors cannot be overloaded.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quicksort on an already sorted array when always choosing the last element as pivot?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Worst-case Quicksort creates 0 and (n-1) partitions each step, yielding O(n^2) time complexity.

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms guarantee O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both Merge Sort (A) and Heap Sort (B) run in O(n log n) worst-case; Insertion Sort is O(n^2) worst-case.

questions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST) with distinct keys, which traversal always visits all keys in ascending sorted order?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Inorder traversal (Left → Root → Right) visits BST keys in strictly ascending order.

questions.question: In an AVL height-balanced binary search tree, what is the maximum allowed magnitude of the balance factor at any node?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Every AVL node must have balance factor in {-1, 0, +1}, so the maximum magnitude is 1.

questions.question: Which statements are true for a Circular Queue implemented using an array of size N?

options.A: Eliminates the wasted front space (false overflow) of a linear array queue
options.B: Distinguishing full vs empty needs keeping 1 slot unused or a separate count
options.C: Front and rear indices wrap around using modulo N arithmetic
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements (A, B, and C) are standard properties of array-based circular queues.

questions.question: What is the worst-case (non-expected) search time complexity in a randomized Skip List containing n elements?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: While average/expected Skip List search is O(log n), the worst-case time complexity is O(n).

questions.question: Which data structure is standardly used to evaluate a postfix (Reverse Polish) arithmetic expression?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Stack stores operands during postfix evaluation and pops two operands whenever an operator is scanned.

questions.question: In a B-Tree of order m = 5 (Knuth definition), every non-root internal node must have at least how many children?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A non-root internal node in an order-m B-Tree must have at least ceil(m/2) children; for m=5, ceil(5/2) = 3 children.

questions.question: Which of the following hash collision resolution methods belong to Open Addressing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Linear probing, quadratic probing, and double hashing are all Open Addressing (closed hashing) techniques.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (where a single-node tree has height 0)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Minimum nodes in a binary tree of height h is h + 1 (skewed tree); 2^(h+1) - 1 is the maximum number of nodes.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of finding the minimum element in a Min-Heap of n elements?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a Min-Heap, the minimum key is always stored at the root (index 0), so finding it takes O(1) time.

questions.question: Which statements are true about standard array Merge Sort?

options.A: It is a stable sorting algorithm
options.B: It follows the Divide and Conquer paradigm
options.C: It sorts in-place using only O(1) auxiliary space
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Merge Sort is stable (A) and uses Divide and Conquer (B), though standard array Merge Sort needs O(n) extra space.

questions.question: Which graph algorithm uses a Queue data structure to find shortest paths (by edge count) in unweighted graphs?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Breadth-First Search (BFS) uses a Queue and guarantees shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

questions.question: Which invariants hold for every valid Red-Black tree?

options.A: Every node is colored either red or black
options.B: The root node is always black
options.C: No red node can have a red child (no two consecutive reds)
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three (A, B, and C) are fundamental Red-Black tree properties.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching for a key in a separate-chaining hash table storing n keys in m buckets?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: If all n keys collide into a single bucket's linked list, worst-case search degrades to O(n).

questions.question: In the 5-state process model, a Running process that initiates a blocking disk I/O read transitions directly to which state?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A process waiting for I/O or an event transitions from Running to the Waiting (Blocked) state.

questions.question: Which of the following belong to the four necessary Coffman conditions for a deadlock to occur?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All four Coffman conditions (mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait) appear across A, B, C.

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm is known for causing the 'convoy effect' when short jobs wait behind one long CPU-bound job?

options.B: Round Robin (RR) with small time quantum
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) suffers from the convoy effect because it is non-preemptive and ignores burst length.

questions.question: In a paged system without parallel lookup, if TLB access takes 10 ns and RAM access takes 100 ns, what is the access time on a TLB HIT?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: On a TLB hit, time = TLB lookup (10 ns) + 1 RAM access for data (100 ns) = 110 ns (210 ns is for a TLB miss).

questions.question: Which statements accurately describe Thrashing in virtual memory systems?

options.A: The system spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions
options.B: CPU utilization plunges sharply when multiprogramming exceeds available frames
options.C: It can be controlled using Denning's Working Set model
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements (A, B, and C) accurately describe thrashing and its Working Set mitigation.

questions.question: Which disk file allocation method suffers from external fragmentation and makes dynamic file growth difficult?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Contiguous allocation stores files in consecutive disk blocks, causing external fragmentation and fixed-size growth limits.

questions.question: Which page replacement algorithm can exhibit Belady's Anomaly (more frames yielding more page faults)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: FIFO is not a stack algorithm and suffers from Belady's Anomaly; LRU and Optimal are stack algorithms and never do.

questions.question: In the Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance, how is the remaining Need[i] vector calculated for process i?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Banker's Algorithm, Need[i] = Max[i] - Allocation[i]. None of A/B/C uses the correct formula.

questions.question: Which statements correctly compare Threads and Processes within an operating system?

options.A: Threads in the same process share code, global data, and open files
options.B: Each thread maintains its own stack, registers, and program counter
options.C: Thread context switching is faster than switching full processes
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three (A, B, and C) are true characteristics of threads compared to heavyweight processes.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) in an OS/MMU?

options.A: Buffer dirty disk blocks before swap write-back
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The TLB is an associative hardware cache that stores recent page table entries (virtual-to-physical frame mappings).

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm achieves the provably minimum average waiting time for a fixed set of processes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SJF (and preemptive SRTF) yields the minimum possible average waiting time for a given set of jobs.

questions.question: Internal fragmentation is an inherent issue in which of the following memory management schemes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Paging and fixed-size partitioning suffer from internal fragmentation; variable partitioning and pure segmentation cause external fragmentation.

questions.question: Which statements are true about a binary semaphore initialized to 1?

options.A: wait() / P() decrements it to 0 or blocks if it is already 0
options.B: signal() / V() wakes a blocked process or sets the value back to 1
options.C: Its integer value can grow arbitrarily above 1 on repeated signal() calls
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both A and B describe a binary semaphore (values restricted to 0 and 1); growing above 1 applies to a counting semaphore.

questions.question: In POSIX/UNIX systems, which system call creates a new child process by duplicating the calling parent process?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: fork() creates a duplicate child process; exec() replaces the current process's memory image.

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm is strictly guaranteed to be free from starvation?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SJF, SRTF, and static priority without aging can all starve long/low-priority jobs; FCFS and Round Robin are starvation-free.

questions.question: In the 7-layer OSI model, which layer provides end-to-end reliability, segmentation, and port addressing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Transport layer (Layer 4) handles segmentation, port numbers, flow control, and end-to-end reliability.

questions.question: What are the standard well-known TCP port numbers for HTTP, HTTPS, and SSH, respectively?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Correct ports are HTTP = 80, HTTPS = 443, and SSH = 22 (port 23 is Telnet).

questions.question: Which statements are true regarding IPv4 and IPv6 addressing?

options.A: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses typically written in dotted-decimal format
options.B: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses written in colon-separated hexadecimal
options.C: IPv6 removes the header checksum field to streamline router forwarding
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements (A, B, and C) accurately describe IPv4 and IPv6 specifications.

questions.question: In classful IPv4 addressing, what are the default subnet mask and first-octet range for Class B networks?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class B uses default mask 255.255.0.0 and first-octet range 128–191 (192–223 is Class C).

questions.question: In Stop-and-Wait ARQ, if link bandwidth is 1 Mbps and round-trip delay is 40 ms, what is the sender window size?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Stop-and-Wait ARQ always has a sender window size of exactly 1 frame regardless of bandwidth or delay.

questions.question: Which statements are true about CSMA/CD (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection)?

options.A: Used in classic wired IEEE 802.3 Ethernet LANs
options.B: Nodes sense the channel before transmitting and abort on collision
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both A and B are true for CSMA/CD; IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA (Collision Avoidance), not CSMA/CD.

questions.question: In CSMA/CD, what minimum frame transmission time Tt (relative to one-way propagation delay Tp) ensures collision detection?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: CSMA/CD requires Tt >= 2 × Tp (one round-trip propagation time) to reliably detect collisions.

questions.question: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address into its corresponding physical MAC address on a local Ethernet LAN?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps an IPv4 address to a MAC address; RARP maps MAC to IP.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols operate at the Application Layer of the TCP/IP suite?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, FTP, SNMP, and DHCP are all TCP/IP Application Layer protocols.

questions.question: In Go-Back-N ARQ using an n-bit sequence number field, what is the maximum allowed sender window size?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Go-Back-N allows up to 2^n - 1 unacknowledged frames; Selective Repeat allows up to 2^(n - 1).

questions.question: Which of the following propositional logic formulas is a TAUTOLOGY (always TRUE)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three formulas (A, B, and C) are contradictions (always FALSE), not tautologies.

questions.question: Which theorems hold for every simple connected planar graph G with v >= 3 vertices, e edges, and f faces?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three (Euler's formula, e <= 3v - 6, and 4-colorability) are true theorems for simple connected planar graphs.

questions.question: A connected undirected graph possesses an Eulerian circuit (closed Eulerian trail) if and only if:

options.A: Exactly two vertices have odd degree
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An Eulerian circuit exists iff every vertex has EVEN degree; exactly 2 odd vertices gives an open Eulerian path.

questions.question: According to Kuratowski's theorem, which of the following graphs is NON-PLANAR?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: K3, K4, and K2,3 are all planar; the minimal non-planar graphs are K5 and K3,3.

questions.question: Which statements are equivalent properties of every Tree on n vertices?

options.A: It is connected and contains no cycles
options.C: Every pair of vertices is joined by a unique simple path
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three (A, B, and C) are equivalent textbook characterizations of an n-vertex tree.

questions.question: For the conditional proposition 'p → q', which expression represents its contrapositive?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The contrapositive of p → q is ¬q → ¬p (A is converse, B is inverse, C is negation).

questions.question: How many edges are present in a simple complete undirected graph K_n with n vertices?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Every pair among n vertices shares one edge, giving C(n, 2) = n(n - 1) / 2 edges.

questions.question: By Dirac's theorem, a simple graph with n >= 3 vertices is guaranteed to have a Hamiltonian cycle if:

options.B: The sum of all vertex degrees is >= n
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Dirac's theorem guarantees a Hamiltonian cycle if every vertex has degree >= n / 2.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid logical equivalences in propositional logic?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three (De Morgan's law, implication identity, and negation of implication) are valid equivalences.

questions.question: In a network of 6 routers connected in a full-mesh topology, how many point-to-point links are needed?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A full mesh of n nodes needs n(n - 1) / 2 links: 6 × 5 / 2 = 15 links.
